## Overview

This adds an oracle benchmark for #61024. It uses saved target-model output as draft tokens, so users can compare real draft methods with reference replay on the same prompts.

## Claims

- A baseline run saves the reference output. Separate runs compare baseline, oracle, ngram, and EAGLE3 throughput.
- Each run saves throughput, draft acceptance, and exact output matches to JSON. The oracle uses the existing `custom_class` interface, with no engine changes.
- The oracle also includes the fix from @dilberx's review. If tokens repeat in the reference, it uses the nearest match instead of the last one. This fixes the reported jump past useful draft tokens.

## Validation

**Scope:** the GPU tests below ran on engine base `5fa7b7b`. The benchmark and test files are unchanged. Local pre-commit checks passed at `6c370bbb5`; GPU tests have not been rerun on the current branch.

Five regression tests ran on one H100 SXM 80GB. Four check repeated matches and ties. One uses OPT-125m to check the output tokens and confirm that draft tokens are accepted.

| Benchmark source | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Before the match fix | 4 failed, 1 passed |
| After the match fix | 5 passed |

The performance comparison used Qwen3-8B on the same H100: BF16, TP=1, greedy output, and at most 384 output tokens. Thinking mode and async scheduling were off. Each setup ran three times, for **27 successful runs** in total.

Values below are median output tokens/s. `k` is the draft length; the cap is `max_num_seqs`, not a fixed batch size.

| Concurrency cap | k | Baseline | Old oracle | Fixed oracle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1, serial | 12 | 123.70 | 456.91 | 478.97 |
| 8 | 12 | 894.87 | 4325.28 | 4560.13 |
| 32 | 16 | 2795.72 | 9295.55 | 9334.39 |

Median throughput rose by 4.8% at cap 1 and 5.4% at cap 8. At cap 32, the 0.4% difference is within run variation, so there is no clear gain.

Outputs and their lengths differed in some runs. The throughput numbers therefore do not compare identical outputs in every case. Exact output matches do not measure task accuracy, and the benchmark does not explain the differences. Draft lengths were fixed; this was not a search for the best configuration.

The last GitHub CI run stopped at the contributor eligibility check before tests could run. It is separate from the H100 and local results above.

<details>
<summary>Run ranges, output checks, and reproduction</summary>

Each row below shows the minimum and maximum throughput across three runs, in output tokens/s.

| Cap | Baseline | Old oracle | Fixed oracle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 120.87–124.10 | 454.76–461.12 | 469.43–488.09 |
| 8 | 889.64–905.97 | 4213.23–4334.91 | 4357.53–4565.44 |
| 32 | 2770.84–2835.09 | 8716.91–9516.97 | 9068.25–9510.74 |

Serial runs used the first 24 prompts; caps 8 and 32 used all 224. Each cap used a reference from its first baseline run. Two warm-up prompts were excluded from the timed pass. The second repeat reversed the old/fixed order.

Old and fixed outputs matched on 24/24 serial prompts in every repeat. At cap 8, the counts were 148, 148, and 131 out of 224. At cap 32, they were 222, 222, and 137 out of 224. Output lengths also varied in some runs.

Against the saved baseline reference, the fixed oracle matched 8/24, 137/224, and 131/224 outputs at caps 1, 8, and 32 in each repeat. These counts measure exact token equality, not task accuracy.

GPU test environment:

- Old benchmark source: `bae2347`; fixed source: `e1ece05`, now rebased as `6c370bbb5`.
- Engine source and official CUDA wheel base: `5fa7b7b01bba4d4e9cd17a4036113d97d086bb8a`.
- Local checks passed at `6c370bbb5`, rebased onto `7495e9e5`. The later main update at `56e518b5` changed only ROCm and CI files; those local checks were not repeated after it.
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B at `b968826d9c46dd6066d109eabc6255188de91218`.
- Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers 5.20.2, FlashInfer 0.7.2.
- Model runner V1 for all modes, maximum model length 4096, GPU memory utilization 0.85.
- Prompts: `prompts.json` in the [original experiment archive](https://gist.github.com/jiangLLM/e95756b974f385846e4277b7ee68d6c8). SHA-256: `331f257ab6897498c031b17304d0f357307e8478bdaadcd7556215371a55d4ce`.

Regression command, run with the same new test file against both benchmark versions:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/benchmarks/test_spec_decode_oracle.py -v -s
```

For example, the old source selected `[9, 20, 21]` where the test expected `[3, 4, 5]`. In the LLM test, it produced the expected output but accepted zero draft tokens. Both cases pass with the fix.

To reproduce the cap-8 comparison, use the tested engine base, the model revision above, and the archived prompts:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"

.venv/bin/python benchmarks/benchmark_spec_decode_oracle.py \
  --model /root/models/Qwen3-8B --mode baseline --prompts prompts.json \
  --max-num-seqs 8 --max-tokens 384 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --no-async-scheduling --write-ref ref.json --out baseline.json

.venv/bin/python benchmarks/benchmark_spec_decode_oracle.py \
  --model /root/models/Qwen3-8B --mode oracle --k 12 --prompts prompts.json \
  --max-num-seqs 8 --max-tokens 384 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --no-async-scheduling --ref ref.json --write-ref oracle-tokens.json \
  --out oracle.json
```

Run the oracle command with the old and fixed benchmark source in the same engine environment. Keep the first baseline reference for all repeats and use separate output paths.

For cap 1, add `--serial --num-prompts 24` and set `--max-num-seqs 1`. For cap 32, use `--max-num-seqs 32 --k 16`. Run each setup three times and reverse the old/fixed order in the second repeat.

Post-rebase check:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  benchmarks/benchmark_spec_decode_oracle.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_spec_decode_oracle.py \
  benchmarks/README.md docs/benchmarking/cli.md \
  .buildkite/test_areas/benchmarks.yaml
```

The original archive includes ngram and EAGLE3 results on vLLM 0.31.0. Those runs predate this fix and were not repeated for it.

</details>

## Details

If output differs from the saved reference, the oracle uses its last three tokens to find a place to resume. When there is more than one match, it selects the match whose end is nearest to the current output length. Ties favor the earlier match. Use `--strict` to disable this rule.

This remains a heuristic. Replay takes CPU time, and draft tokens can be rejected, so the oracle is a measured performance reference rather than a theoretical upper bound.

AI assistance: Claude helped draft the original script. Codex prepared the fix, ran the validation, and handled the rebase.

nodes.body: Hi @benchislett, this PR adds a reference-replay benchmark for the oracle verification task listed in #61024. Could you review it when you get a chance? Thanks!!

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @jiangLLM.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

If the 3-gram appears more than once in `ref`, this jumps to the last copy, which can be far past where the generation is. Code outputs repeat 3-grams a lot (indentation, `return`). With `ref = [1, 2, A, B, C, 3, 4, 5, A, B, C, 6, 7, 8, A, B, C, 9, 20, 21]` and `gen = [1, 99, A, B, C]`, it resyncs to 17 and drafts `[9, 20, 21]` where the next tokens should be `[3, 4, 5]`. Every later step for that request goes through `_resync` too, so the oracle numbers come out low. Taking the match closest to `len(gen)` fixes it:

```suggestion
        end = int(idx[np.argmin(np.abs(idx + m - len(gen)))]) + m
```

+"""Benchmark speculative decoding with a reference-replay oracle.

+The oracle replays saved target-model outputs as draft tokens. Comparing it
+with ngram and EAGLE3 provides a performance reference for the tested setup.
+Replay has nonzero CPU overhead, and proposals may be rejected, so the result
+is not a theoretical upper bound.

+        --mode baseline --prompts prompts.json --max-num-seqs 32 \
+        --no-async-scheduling --write-ref ref.json --out base.json
+    # 2. reference-replay oracle at k=4

+        --mode oracle --k 4 --prompts prompts.json --max-num-seqs 32 \
+        --ref ref.json --out oracle_k4.json
+    # 3. a real drafter for comparison
+    python benchmarks/benchmark_spec_decode_oracle.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
+        --mode eagle3 --k 3 --draft-model RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3 \
+        --prompts prompts.json --max-num-seqs 32 --no-async-scheduling \
+        --ref ref.json --out e3.json
+
+Use ``--no-async-scheduling`` on the baseline and EAGLE3 to match the scheduling
+mode used by CPU-side drafters (``custom_class``, ``ngram``).
+
+``--prompts`` is a JSON list of user-turn strings; the chat template is
+applied with thinking disabled for Qwen3 models.
+"""

+import argparse
+import glob
+import json
+import os
+import time

+import numpy as np

+# The oracle is loaded by vLLM's custom_class proposer via this module path,
+# so the benchmarks directory must be importable (it is when the script is
+# run from the repository root or by path).
+ORACLE_CLASS = "benchmark_spec_decode_oracle.OracleProposer"
+
+
+class OracleProposer:
+    """Drafter that replays a reference output for each request.
+
+    The reference file (``ORACLE_REF_FILE``) is a JSON list of
+    ``{"prompt_token_ids": [...], "output_token_ids": [...]}`` written by a
+    ``--mode baseline`` run. Requests are identified by the bytes of their
+    first ``L`` prompt tokens, where ``L`` is the shortest prompt length.
+
+    While generation matches the reference, up to ``k`` reference tokens
+    are proposed. If the output diverges, the proposer attempts to realign
+    using the last ``ORACLE_RESYNC_NGRAM`` (3) generated tokens in the reference.
+    ``ORACLE_STRICT=1`` disables realignment, so divergent requests receive
+    no drafts. Cumulative proposer statistics are written to
+    ``ORACLE_STATS_DIR/oracle_stats_<pid>.json`` every 100 calls. These snapshots
+    include warm-up, may omit the final calls, and can be absent for short runs.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, vllm_config):
+        spec = vllm_config.speculative_config
+        self.k = int(spec.num_speculative_tokens)
+        self.max_model_len = int(vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len)
+        self.strict = os.environ.get("ORACLE_STRICT", "0") == "1"
+        self.m = int(os.environ.get("ORACLE_RESYNC_NGRAM", "3"))
+        with open(os.environ["ORACLE_REF_FILE"]) as f:
+            refs = json.load(f)
+        self.key_len = min(len(r["prompt_token_ids"]) for r in refs)
+        self.table: dict[bytes, tuple[int, np.ndarray]] = {}
+        for r in refs:
+            prompt = np.asarray(r["prompt_token_ids"], dtype=np.int32)
+            key = prompt[: self.key_len].tobytes()
+            if key in self.table:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"two prompts share their first {self.key_len} tokens; "
+                    "the oracle cannot tell them apart"
+                )
+            out = np.asarray(r["output_token_ids"], dtype=np.int32)
+            self.table[key] = (len(prompt), out)
+        self.counters = {
+            "calls": 0,
+            "rows": 0,
+            "lookup_miss": 0,
+            "on_ref": 0,
+            "diverged": 0,
+            "resynced": 0,
+            "no_resync": 0,
+            "past_end": 0,
+            "drafted_tokens": 0,
+        }
+        self.time_s = 0.0
+        stats_dir = os.environ.get("ORACLE_STATS_DIR", "/tmp")
+        self.stats_path = os.path.join(stats_dir, f"oracle_stats_{os.getpid()}.json")
+
+    def _flush_stats(self) -> None:
+        stats: dict[str, object] = dict(self.counters)
+        stats.update(
+            pid=os.getpid(),
+            time_s=round(self.time_s, 4),
+            ms_per_call=round(1000 * self.time_s / max(1, self.counters["calls"]), 4),
+            key_len=self.key_len,
+            strict=self.strict,
+            resync_ngram=self.m,
+        )
+        try:
+            with open(self.stats_path, "w") as f:
+                json.dump(stats, f)
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+
+    def _resync(self, gen: np.ndarray, ref: np.ndarray) -> int | None:
+        """Return the index in ``ref`` after the last match of ``gen[-m:]``."""
+        m = self.m
+        if len(gen) < m or len(ref) <= m:
+            return None
+        gram = gen[-m:]
+        n = len(ref) - m + 1
+        hits = np.ones(n, dtype=bool)
+        for j in range(m):
+            hits &= ref[j : j + n] == gram[j]
+        idx = np.flatnonzero(hits)
+        if idx.size == 0:
+            return None
+        end = int(idx[-1]) + m

export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"

If output differs from the saved reference, the oracle uses its last three tokens to find a place to resume. When there is more than one match, it selects the match whose end is nearest to the current output length. Ties favor the earlier match. Use `--strict` to disable this rule.

This remains a heuristic. Replay takes CPU time, and draft tokens can be rejected, so the oracle is a measured performance reference rather than a theoretical upper bound.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Benchmark speculative decoding with a reference-replay oracle.
+
+The oracle replays saved target-model outputs as draft tokens. Comparing it
+with ngram and EAGLE3 provides a performance reference for the tested setup.
+Replay has nonzero CPU overhead, and proposals may be rejected, so the result
+is not a theoretical upper bound.
+
+Typical use (one configuration per process; see benchmarks/README.md):
+
+    # 1. baseline, also writes the reference outputs the oracle replays
+    python benchmarks/benchmark_spec_decode_oracle.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
+        --mode baseline --prompts prompts.json --max-num-seqs 32 \
+        --no-async-scheduling --write-ref ref.json --out base.json
+    # 2. reference-replay oracle at k=4
+    python benchmarks/benchmark_spec_decode_oracle.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
+        --mode oracle --k 4 --prompts prompts.json --max-num-seqs 32 \
+        --ref ref.json --out oracle_k4.json
+    # 3. a real drafter for comparison
+    python benchmarks/benchmark_spec_decode_oracle.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
+        --mode eagle3 --k 3 --draft-model RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3 \
+        --prompts prompts.json --max-num-seqs 32 --no-async-scheduling \
+        --ref ref.json --out e3.json
+
+Use ``--no-async-scheduling`` on the baseline and EAGLE3 to match the scheduling
+mode used by CPU-side drafters (``custom_class``, ``ngram``).
+
+``--prompts`` is a JSON list of user-turn strings; the chat template is
+applied with thinking disabled for Qwen3 models.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import glob
+import json
+import os
+import time
+
+import numpy as np
+
+# The oracle is loaded by vLLM's custom_class proposer via this module path,
+# so the benchmarks directory must be importable (it is when the script is
+# run from the repository root or by path).
+ORACLE_CLASS = "benchmark_spec_decode_oracle.OracleProposer"
+
+
+class OracleProposer:
+    """Drafter that replays a reference output for each request.
+
+    The reference file (``ORACLE_REF_FILE``) is a JSON list of
+    ``{"prompt_token_ids": [...], "output_token_ids": [...]}`` written by a
+    ``--mode baseline`` run. Requests are identified by the bytes of their
+    first ``L`` prompt tokens, where ``L`` is the shortest prompt length.
+
+    While generation matches the reference, up to ``k`` reference tokens
+    are proposed. If the output diverges, the proposer attempts to realign
+    using the last ``ORACLE_RESYNC_NGRAM`` (3) generated tokens in the reference.
+    ``ORACLE_STRICT=1`` disables realignment, so divergent requests receive
+    no drafts. Cumulative proposer statistics are written to
+    ``ORACLE_STATS_DIR/oracle_stats_<pid>.json`` every 100 calls. These snapshots
+    include warm-up, may omit the final calls, and can be absent for short runs.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, vllm_config):
+        spec = vllm_config.speculative_config
+        self.k = int(spec.num_speculative_tokens)
+        self.max_model_len = int(vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len)
+        self.strict = os.environ.get("ORACLE_STRICT", "0") == "1"
+        self.m = int(os.environ.get("ORACLE_RESYNC_NGRAM", "3"))
+        with open(os.environ["ORACLE_REF_FILE"]) as f:
+            refs = json.load(f)
+        self.key_len = min(len(r["prompt_token_ids"]) for r in refs)
+        self.table: dict[bytes, tuple[int, np.ndarray]] = {}
+        for r in refs:
+            prompt = np.asarray(r["prompt_token_ids"], dtype=np.int32)
+            key = prompt[: self.key_len].tobytes()
+            if key in self.table:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"two prompts share their first {self.key_len} tokens; "
+                    "the oracle cannot tell them apart"
+                )
+            out = np.asarray(r["output_token_ids"], dtype=np.int32)
+            self.table[key] = (len(prompt), out)
+        self.counters = {
+            "calls": 0,
+            "rows": 0,
+            "lookup_miss": 0,
+            "on_ref": 0,
+            "diverged": 0,
+            "resynced": 0,
+            "no_resync": 0,
+            "past_end": 0,
+            "drafted_tokens": 0,
+        }
+        self.time_s = 0.0
+        stats_dir = os.environ.get("ORACLE_STATS_DIR", "/tmp")
+        self.stats_path = os.path.join(stats_dir, f"oracle_stats_{os.getpid()}.json")
+
+    def _flush_stats(self) -> None:
+        stats: dict[str, object] = dict(self.counters)
+        stats.update(
+            pid=os.getpid(),
+            time_s=round(self.time_s, 4),
+            ms_per_call=round(1000 * self.time_s / max(1, self.counters["calls"]), 4),
+            key_len=self.key_len,
+            strict=self.strict,
+            resync_ngram=self.m,
+        )
+        try:
+            with open(self.stats_path, "w") as f:
+                json.dump(stats, f)
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+
+    def _resync(self, gen: np.ndarray, ref: np.ndarray) -> int | None:
+        """Return the match end in ``ref`` nearest to the current output length."""
+        m = self.m
+        if len(gen) < m or len(ref) <= m:
+            return None
+        gram = gen[-m:]
+        n = len(ref) - m + 1
+        hits = np.ones(n, dtype=bool)
+        for j in range(m):
+            hits &= ref[j : j + n] == gram[j]
+        idx = np.flatnonzero(hits)
+        if idx.size == 0:
+            return None
+        end = int(idx[np.argmin(np.abs(idx + m - len(gen)))]) + m
+        return end if end < len(ref) else None
+
+    def propose(
+        self,
+        sampled_token_ids: list[list[int]],
+        num_tokens_no_spec: np.ndarray,
+        token_ids_cpu: np.ndarray,
+        slot_mappings=None,
+    ) -> list[list[int]]:
+        """Propose up to ``k`` reference tokens for eligible requests."""
+        t0 = time.perf_counter()
+        c = self.counters
+        c["calls"] += 1
+        k, key_len = self.k, self.key_len
+        drafts: list[list[int]] = []
+        for i, sampled in enumerate(sampled_token_ids):
+            if not sampled:
+                drafts.append([])
+                continue
+            c["rows"] += 1
+            n = int(num_tokens_no_spec[i])
+            if n >= self.max_model_len or n < key_len:
+                drafts.append([])
+                continue
+            row = token_ids_cpu[i]
+            key = row[:key_len].astype(np.int32, copy=False).tobytes()
+            hit = self.table.get(key)
+            if hit is None:
+                c["lookup_miss"] += 1
+                drafts.append([])
+                continue
+            prompt_len, ref = hit
+            pos = n - prompt_len
+            if pos < 0 or pos >= len(ref):
+                c["past_end"] += 1
+                drafts.append([])
+                continue
+            gen = row[prompt_len:n]
+            if np.array_equal(gen, ref[:pos]):
+                c["on_ref"] += 1
+                start = pos
+            else:
+                c["diverged"] += 1
+                resynced = None if self.strict else self._resync(gen, ref)
+                if resynced is None:
+                    c["no_resync"] += 1
+                    drafts.append([])
+                    continue
+                c["resynced"] += 1
+                start = resynced
+            draft = ref[start : start + k].tolist()
+            c["drafted_tokens"] += len(draft)
+            drafts.append(draft)
+        self.time_s += time.perf_counter() - t0
+        if c["calls"] % 100 == 0:
+            self._flush_stats()
+        return drafts
+
+
+def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
+    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
+    p.add_argument("--model", required=True)
+    p.add_argument(
+        "--mode", required=True, choices=["baseline", "oracle", "ngram", "eagle3"]
+    )
+    p.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=0, help="num_speculative_tokens")
+    p.add_argument("--draft-model", default=None, help="EAGLE3 draft head")
+    p.add_argument("--prompts", required=True, help="JSON list of prompt strings")
+    p.add_argument("--num-prompts", type=int, default=0, help="0 = all")
+    p.add_argument("--ref", default=None, help="reference outputs from a baseline run")
+    p.add_argument("--write-ref", default=None, help="baseline: write reference here")
+    p.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true", help="oracle: stop on divergence")
+    p.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=256)
+    p.add_argument("--max-model-len", type=int, default=4096)
+    p.add_argument("--max-num-seqs", type=int, default=32)
+    p.add_argument(
+        "--serial", action="store_true", help="send prompts one at a time (bs=1)"
+    )
+    p.add_argument(
+        "--no-async-scheduling",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="force async_scheduling=False; use on the baseline the oracle is "
+        "compared against, since vLLM disables it for CPU-side drafters",
+    )
+    p.add_argument("--gpu-memory-utilization", type=float, default=0.85)
+    p.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="result JSON path")
+    p.add_argument("--tag", default="", help="free-form label stored in the result")
+    return p.parse_args()
+
+
+def build_prompts(model: str, prompts_path: str, num_prompts: int) -> list[list[int]]:
+    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+    with open(prompts_path) as f:
+        texts = json.load(f)
+    if num_prompts:
+        texts = texts[:num_prompts]
+    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model)
+    kwargs = {"enable_thinking": False} if "qwen3" in model.lower() else {}
+    prompt_ids = []
+    for text in texts:
+        ids = tok.apply_chat_template(
+            [{"role": "user", "content": text}],
+            add_generation_prompt=True,
+            tokenize=True,
+            **kwargs,
+        )
+        if hasattr(ids, "input_ids"):
+            ids = ids["input_ids"]
+        prompt_ids.append([int(t) for t in ids])
+    return prompt_ids
+
+
+def speculative_config(args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict | None:
+    if args.mode == "baseline":
+        return None
+    if args.mode == "oracle":
+        if not args.ref:
+            raise SystemExit("--ref is required for --mode oracle")
+        os.environ["ORACLE_REF_FILE"] = args.ref
+        os.environ["ORACLE_STRICT"] = "1" if args.strict else "0"
+        stats_dir = f"/tmp/oracle_stats_{os.getpid()}"
+        os.makedirs(stats_dir, exist_ok=True)
+        os.environ["ORACLE_STATS_DIR"] = stats_dir
+        return {
+            "method": "custom_class",
+            "model": ORACLE_CLASS,
+            "num_speculative_tokens": args.k,
+        }
+    if args.mode == "ngram":
+        return {
+            "method": "ngram",
+            "num_speculative_tokens": args.k,
+            "prompt_lookup_max": 5,
+            "prompt_lookup_min": 3,
+        }
+    if not args.draft_model:
+        raise SystemExit("--draft-model is required for --mode eagle3")
+    return {
+        "method": "eagle3",
+        "model": args.draft_model,
+        "num_speculative_tokens": args.k,
+    }
+
+
+def spec_decode_metrics(llm) -> dict:
+    """Collect the spec-decode counters exposed by ``LLM.get_metrics()``."""
+    out: dict = {}
+    for m in llm.get_metrics():
+        name = getattr(m, "name", "")
+        if "spec_decode" not in name:
+            continue
+        if hasattr(m, "value"):
+            out[name] = out.get(name, 0) + m.value
+        elif hasattr(m, "values"):
+            out[name] = list(m.values)
+    return out
+
+
+def subtract(after: dict, before: dict) -> dict:
+    delta: dict = {}
+    for name, v in after.items():
+        b = before.get(name)
+        if isinstance(v, list):
+            if isinstance(b, list) and len(b) == len(v):
+                delta[name] = [x - y for x, y in zip(v, b)]
+            else:
+                delta[name] = v
+        elif isinstance(v, (int, float)):
+            delta[name] = v - (b if isinstance(b, (int, float)) else 0)
+        else:
+            delta[name] = v
+    return delta
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    args = parse_args()
+    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+    from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt
+
+    prompt_ids = build_prompts(args.model, args.prompts, args.num_prompts)
+    spec = speculative_config(args)
+
+    t_init = time.time()
+    llm = LLM(
+        model=args.model,
+        dtype="bfloat16",
+        max_model_len=args.max_model_len,
+        max_num_seqs=args.max_num_seqs,
+        gpu_memory_utilization=args.gpu_memory_utilization,
+        speculative_config=spec,
+        disable_log_stats=False,
+        seed=0,
+        # None lets vLLM choose the scheduling mode for this configuration.
+        async_scheduling=False if args.no_async_scheduling else None,
+    )
+    init_s = time.time() - t_init
+
+    sampling = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=args.max_tokens)
+    inputs = [TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=ids) for ids in prompt_ids]
+
+    # Warm-up is not timed and its spec-decode counters are subtracted.
+    llm.generate(inputs[:2], sampling, use_tqdm=False)
+    before = spec_decode_metrics(llm)
+
+    per_request_latency: list[float] = []
+    t0 = time.time()
+    if args.serial:
+        outputs = []
+        for inp in inputs:
+            t = time.time()
+            outputs.append(llm.generate([inp], sampling, use_tqdm=False)[0])
+            per_request_latency.append(time.time() - t)
+    else:
+        outputs = llm.generate(inputs, sampling, use_tqdm=False)
+    wall = time.time() - t0
+
+    out_ids = [list(o.outputs[0].token_ids) for o in outputs]
+    n_out = sum(len(x) for x in out_ids)
+    metrics = subtract(spec_decode_metrics(llm), before)
+
+    result = {
+        "tag": args.tag,
+        "mode": args.mode,
+        "k": args.k,
+        "model": args.model,
+        "draft_model": args.draft_model,
+        "strict_oracle": bool(args.strict) if args.mode == "oracle" else None,
+        "async_scheduling_forced_off": args.no_async_scheduling,
+        "num_prompts": len(inputs),
+        "serial": args.serial,
+        "max_num_seqs": args.max_num_seqs,
+        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
+        "init_s": round(init_s, 1),
+        "wall_s": round(wall, 3),
+        "output_tokens": n_out,
+        "tokens_per_s": round(n_out / wall, 2),
+        "mean_output_len": round(n_out / max(1, len(inputs)), 1),
+        "spec_metrics": metrics,
+    }
+    if per_request_latency:
+        lat = sorted(per_request_latency)
+        result["req_latency_mean_s"] = round(sum(lat) / len(lat), 3)
+        result["req_latency_p50_s"] = round(lat[len(lat) // 2], 3)
+        # Generation wall time per output token, including prefill.
+        result["tpot_ms"] = round(1000 * wall / max(1, n_out), 2)
+
+    drafts = metrics.get("vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts", 0)
+    draft_tokens = metrics.get("vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens", 0)
+    accepted = metrics.get("vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens", 0)
+    if drafts:
+        # Mean accepted draft tokens per draft event, plus the bonus token.
+        result["mean_acceptance_len"] = round(1 + accepted / drafts, 3)
+        result["draft_acceptance_rate"] = round(accepted / max(1, draft_tokens), 4)
+
+    if args.mode == "oracle":
+        stats = []
+        for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(os.environ["ORACLE_STATS_DIR"], "*.json")):
+            with open(path) as f:
+                stats.append(json.load(f))
+        result["oracle_proposer_stats"] = stats
+
+    if args.ref:
+        with open(args.ref) as f:
+            refs = json.load(f)
+        ref_map = {tuple(r["prompt_token_ids"]): r["output_token_ids"] for r in refs}
+        same = sum(1 for p, o in zip(prompt_ids, out_ids) if ref_map.get(tuple(p)) == o)
+        result["outputs_identical_to_ref"] = same
+        result["outputs_identical_frac"] = round(same / len(out_ids), 3)
+
+    if args.write_ref:
+        with open(args.write_ref, "w") as f:
+            json.dump(
+                [
+                    {"prompt_token_ids": p, "output_token_ids": o}
+                    for p, o in zip(prompt_ids, out_ids)
+                ],
+                f,
+            )
+
+    with open(args.out, "w") as f:
+        json.dump(result, f, indent=1)
+    print("RESULT", json.dumps(result))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+    using the last ``ORACLE_RESYNC_NGRAM`` (3) generated tokens in the reference.
